title: What to watch at the open
text: Today's big story is NVIDIA. Reports say its board met late Wednesday to talk about whether CEO Jensen Huang should keep his job, and no decision had been announced this morning. NVIDIA closed Wednesday at $173.73, but it fell roughly 7% to 9% in trading outside normal hours. That would put it below its lowest price of the past year ($164.27). Nasdaq futures, which are bets on where the index will open, pointed lower. Watch whether the drop spreads to other AI names, or whether money moves from NVIDIA into rivals like AMD and Broadcom, which rose after hours.

title: NVIDIA could open near a one year low
text: NVIDIA is the biggest company on our list. Early trading suggests it could open around $158 to $162, under its 52 week low of $164.27. Analysts also cut their average price target from $340 to about $329 in a day. Big moves before the open can shrink or grow once the full market starts trading at 9:30 a.m.

title: AMD is up 7% and near the top of its range
text: AMD jumped 7.3% on Wednesday to $552.90. It now sits at about 78% of its one year range, while NVIDIA sits at about 12%. Two chip companies that make similar products can move in opposite directions when news is about one company and not the whole industry.

title: Inflation data is still in the background
text: Tuesday's inflation report came in hotter than expected, and one Federal Reserve official said he leans toward raising interest rates in December. Another report on prices that businesses pay, called the producer price index, is due Friday. Higher rates can weigh on fast growing tech stocks.

title: Lesson 48: What is a board of directors?
text: Every public company has a board of directors. It is a small group of people elected by the shareholders, the people who own the stock. The board does not run the company day to day. That is the CEO's job. Instead, the board watches over the CEO, sets the CEO's pay, and can hire or fire the CEO. Think of a school: the principal runs the school every day, but the school board can replace the principal. When a board starts talking about removing a famous CEO, investors get nervous because they do not know who will lead next or what will change.

title: What this covers
text: Prices are from Wednesday's close, November 11. Price targets and company ratios come from FMP for NVIDIA, TSMC, AMD, Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta, Lockheed Martin and GE Aerospace. Broadcom, Vertiv, Rocket Lab, Eli Lilly and Intuitive Surgical show price and risk data only. After hours moves are from news reports and are not part of the closing prices. This is for learning, not advice to buy or sell.
